compensating.why: hop 2 always appends a new element to head
hop 2 appends a new element to body instead of head
hop 3 passes the tag name without lower-casing it

ownership_reason: Only the gold searches the document tree: given root and a tag name it is meant to return the first element with that tag name under root in document order, which in jsoup covers every element under root, not only root's own children. Hop 1 sets the text of the element hop 2 returns; hop 2 chooses between the found element and a new element appended to head; hops 3 and 4 only lower-case and check the tag name. The variant gold looks only at root's own child elements, so for '<title>First</title><title>Ignore</title>' (both titles inside html > head) it returns null, hop 2 appends a new title to head, and the document's first title still reads 'First' after title("Hello"); 'Hello' can come back only if a caller searches the tree itself (a second implementation of the gold's step), narrows the search to head against hop 2's 'anywhere in a document', or removes head's contents against hop 2's documentation. The convention that searching an element for a tag name covers the whole tree under it is pinned outside the gold: Element.getElementsByTag ('including and recursively under this element'), Element.getElementById, Element.select and Document.head (through the recursive findFirstElementByTagName) do the same step in production, and ElementTest::getElementsByTagName (nested div2 found, document order), ElementTest::testGetElementById and ParserTest::createsDocumentStructure pass.
